title: Assurance synthesis: RBAC v2, audit-flow, and evidence automation strategy
body:
Purpose:
This working brief synthesizes our current RBAC v2 rollout, audit-log schema, SIEM export pipeline, and the evidence automation effort into a single control-to-evidence roadmap for SOC 2 and ISO 27001 readiness. The intent is to provide auditors a narrative and quick answers, and to give engineering owners concrete remediation actions and automation steps to close gaps within the next two quarters.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: RBAC v2 (authorization model changes), audit-log schema (fields & retention), SIEM export (format, delivery, transforms), evidence automation (ingest, validation, packaging).
- Audience: Security & compliance, applied-ml infra, serving-runtime, SRE, and external auditors.

Executive summary (one paragraph):
We have implemented the RBAC v2 model for principal-level least-privilege with role inheritance and policy binding. Audit logs exist across control planes (API, infra, console) but schema coverage is inconsistent: key fields required by SOC 2 (actor_identity, action_type, resource_id, success, previous_state_hash) are present in API logs but are partial in console and private-deployments exports. SIEM ingestion is implemented via Kafka -> log-transform -> SIEM connector but lacks consistent parseability for important ISO controls (evidence of change authorization, segmentation of duties). Evidence automation pipelines are scaffolded; automated snapshots exist for token issuance and role-changes but not for long-running policy evaluations or some Dedicated control events. This doc maps out the delta, prioritizes fixes, and prepares a Q&A bundle for auditors.

Current state snapshot (concise):
- RBAC v2: Deployed to hosted API and Console (canary). AuthZ decisions are logged with trace IDs. Role model supports role inheritance, ephemeral grants, and admin delegation. Missing: an immutable changelog entry for policy rationale in the private deployments package.
- Audit-log schema: Canonical schema v0.7 in repo. API logs include: timestamp, actor_id, actor_type, action, resource_type, resource_id, request_id, trace_id, result, error_code, context. Console logs omit resource_type consistently and sometimes omit previous_state for PATCH actions.
- SIEM export: Kafka topic redwood-audit, transform job 'audit-normalizer' writes JSON-L with schema tags, SIEM connector pulls daily batches. Issue: delayed export for private-deployments (buffered file drops) and no deduplication strategy for replays.
- Evidence automation: proof-of-change snapshots generated by the evidence collector (lambda) for hosted API; collector does not automatically attach human approvals or Jira/Linear links.

Control mapping and gap analysis (high-level mapping to SOC 2 / ISO 27001 controls):
- A. Access controls / Authorization (SOC 2 CC6, ISO A.9):
  - Requirement: enforce least privilege, log authorization decisions, demonstrate review processes.
  - Present: RBAC v2 enforces roles; logs capture decision outcomes for API calls.
  - Gap: Private deployments do not emit policy rationales or admin review metadata to audit logs.
  - Remediation priority: High. Ship changelog metadata in policy-manager and include approval references in events.

- B. Audit logging and monitoring (SOC 2 CC7, ISO A.12.4/A.12.6):
  - Requirement: comprehensive, tamper-evident logs with retention and export controls.
  - Present: Central pipeline exists; retention policy defined in doc store.
  - Gap: Missing previous_state for config changes, inconsistent resource_type field, SIEM ingest replay duplication risk, and lack of signed log checksums for Private audit files.
  - Remediation priority: High for signed checksums and previous_state; Medium for replay dedupe.

- C. Change management & evidence of authorization (ISO A.12.1, SOC 2 CP):
  - Requirement: evidence linking change to authorized request and review.
  - Present: Ticket numbers sometimes attached to audits; automated role/grant flows included.
  - Gap: No enforced ticket-to-change binding for console manual edits; no automated capture of reviewer identity for emergency rollbacks.
  - Remediation priority: Medium-High. Add required metadata on console edits and emergency rollback approvals.

- D. SIEM and alerting (ISO A.12.4.1 / SOC 2):
  - Requirement: real-time / near-real-time detection and retention of alerts; structured fields for detection rules.
  - Present: SIEM has baseline rules; export transform supports tagging.
  - Gap: Detection rules do not reference RBAC policy drift metrics; SIEM ingestion lacks canonical "control_id" for traceability to compliance matrix.
  - Remediation priority: Medium.

Concrete remediation actions and owners (with rough ETA):
- Add policy-changelog metadata field to RBAC change events (fields: policy_id, author_id, justification, ticket_ref). Owner: platform-engineering. ETA: 3 weeks for schema, 6 weeks for end-to-end.
- Extend audit-log schema v0.7 -> v0.9 to require previous_state (base64-diff), resource_type, and approver_id where applicable. Owner: observability team. ETA: 4 weeks.
- Implement signed manifest file (SHA256 + key rotation) for Private deployment daily exports. Owner: private-deployments + infra. ETA: 6 weeks.
- SIEM transform: add control_id mapping table and dedupe window (idempotency key = request_id + sequence). Owner: observability. ETA: 3 weeks.
- Evidence automation: attach ticket and PR ids to change snapshots plus attach reviewer signatures (SAML name + time). Owner: security-and-compliance + platform-engineering. ETA: 5 weeks.

Prioritized risk/impact matrix (short):
- Must-fix (blocker for audit signoff): missing previous_state for configuration changes; missing signed manifests for Private exports; missing approver linkage for some high-privilege changes.
- Important (affects evidentiary completeness): inconsistent resource_type and replay dedupe; missing policy-rationale on private.
- Nice-to-have (improves audit speed): SIEM control_id canonicalization; RBAC policy drift telemetry.

Automated evidence packaging runbook (for engineers):
1) Event capture: ensure service emits audit event with schema v0.9 fields.
2) Evidence collector: pull events from Kafka topic redwood-audit; enrich with ticket metadata via the ticket-mapper service.
3) Snapshot packaging: bundle events into daily evidence artifacts with manifest.json (SHA256 per file + signed-manifest.sig).
4) Upload: push to compliance-bucket/tenant/<org-id>/date=YYYY-MM-DD/; set ACL to compliance-readonly.
5) Index: update confluence-indexer with artifact id and control mappings for easy auditor lookup.

Auditor Q&A prep (anticipated questions with suggested answers):
Q1: How do you demonstrate that RBAC role changes were authorized and reviewed?
A1: All RBAC change events include a policy_changelog entry that records author_id, justification, ticket_ref, and approver_id. For hosted API and Console this metadata is mandatory; for Private deployments the next release will emit the same fields and the export manifest will include a signed changelog. Cross-reference: evidence artifact IDs in S3 and confluence index.

Q2: How do you prevent tampering of exported logs for on-prem customers?
A2: Private exports include a daily signed manifest (SHA256 over concatenated files) signed by our infra key. We rotate signing keys quarterly and store public keys in the compliance key registry. Auditors can verify manifests against the public key.

Q3: If a console admin performs an emergency rollback, how is that captured?
A3: Emergency rollbacks are recorded as events with emergency=true, previous_state included, approval metadata attached (approver_id or emergency_waiver_ticket). The policy change coordinator receives an automated notification and the event is flagged in SIEM for immediate review.

Q4: How are logs correlated across services (API, console, runtime)?
A4: We use trace_id and request_id in all service-level events. The audit-normalizer augments events with a canonical correlation_id and a control_id that maps to the compliance matrix. Cross-service joins are reproducible via these IDs.

Q5: What retention and deletion policy applies to evidence artifacts?
A5: Retention defaults to 7 years for control artifacts supporting enterprise contracts; scope-specific shorter retention (e.g., 2 years) is configurable per customer for Private deployments. Deletion requests for personal data follow the data-privacy playbook and generate an audit event that is retained.

Evidence index (representative list of artifacts to present to auditors):
- S3 artifact: compliance-bucket/hosted/2025-02-01/rbac-changelog-20250201.json (contains role deltas + approvals).
- S3 artifact: compliance-bucket/private/2025-02-01/audit-export-manifest.sig (signed manifest).
- SIEM exports: link to daily-export-2025-02-01.ndjson (hash: sha256:abcd1234...).
- Confluence pages: Policy change playbook (CONFLUENCE-PRIV-CHANGES).

Open questions and decisions needed from execs/security:
- Binding policy: Should we require ticket_ref for every console edit (reduces speed for incident triage)? Tradeoff: audit completeness vs operational agility. Recommend: require ticket_ref for non-emergency changes; emergency exemptions logged and require post-facto approval within 24 hours.
- Key custody for Private export signing: use customer-provided public keys (preferred) or Redwood-managed key? Recommend customer-provided where contract allows; otherwise Redwood-managed with strict KMS controls.

Next steps and timeline (two-quarter plan):
- Sprint 1 (0-4 weeks): audit-log schema update; SIEM control_id mapping; policy-changelog schema draft. Owners: observability + platform.
- Sprint 2 (4-8 weeks): implement signed manifests for Private exports; evidence collector enhancements. Owners: private-deployments + infra.
- Sprint 3 (8-12 weeks): attach approver metadata for console edits; enforce ticket_ref policy for non-emergency. Owners: console-and-tooling + security.
- Sprint 4 (12-16 weeks): validation run with internal audit, produce final evidence bundle for auditor preview. Owner: security-and-compliance.

Appendix: quick links and commands engineers can use
- Validate schema locally: python tools/validate_audit_schema.py --file sample-event.json --schema schemas/audit-v0.9.json
- Generate signed manifest locally: tools/sign_manifest.sh compliance-artifact-dir/ --key infra-signing-key.pem
- Evidence collector debug: kubectl logs -n observability evidence-collector-<pod> --since=2h

Contact and escalation:
Owner: Asha Patel (security-and-compliance) — asha.patel@redwood.com
Escalation: Priya Rao (Head of Security) — priya.rao@redwood.com

Notes and working items (short bulleted):
- Discussion items for architects: minimal fields for previous_state (diff vs full snapshot).
- Research: feasible dedupe windows and idempotency guarantees for Kafka replays.
- Follow-up: schedule meeting with Private deployments team for signing key options.

This doc is intentionally a working synthesis for auditors and engineering owners; please add inline comments and mark items you pick up in the linked Jira epic JIRA-SC-78.
